item: GET /api/catalog/export.csv reads the twelve columns it writes, not 86,000 Source entities
refs: entity-load sweep of src/api 2026-10-27; A-025 class (#1522); audit 0.5.0 follow-up
summary: The sources CSV export built a mapped Source instance (24 columns) for every source to write twelve of them. It now asks the database for the twelve columns the row builder reads (_EXPORT_ATTRS, pinned to the builder by a recording stand-in), so no instance is built. Measured on 86,000 synthetic sources, nothing else running, the store seeded in another process: 2.7 to 3.6 s before, 1.7 to 2.0 s after (two benches, 3 runs each, 5 GETs per run); Python allocation peak during the GET 216 MiB before, 124 MiB after (tracemalloc); body 10,084,877 B and sha256 identical. The sweep read 32 chain sites and every query(Model) in src/api: this was the only unbounded entity load of a large table (the rest are page- or id-bounded, or need Article content by design); disable-unmanaged (source_management.py) writes through the ORM and stays a proposal. LIMIT: the store is synthetic (86,000 rows of eight repeated shapes), not the field catalogue.
